ch04.d.theta: Angle between the initial velocity and the horizontal; 0° is a horizontal throw
ch04.d.h: Height of the launch point; 0 is the ground
ch04.d.v0: Speed at the moment of release
ch04.d.vectors: Velocity $v$ on the ball and its components $v_x$, $v_y$ on the shadows
ch04.goal.split: Projectile motion = uniform motion in $x$ + uniformly accelerated motion in $y$ (acceleration $-g$)
ch04.goal.indep: The two motions are independent; they share only the time $t$
ch04.obs.x: Shadow on the $x$ axis: equal distances in equal times (evenly spaced strobe marks), constant $v_x$
ch04.obs.y: Shadow on the $y$ axis: moves like a ball thrown straight up; $v_y = 0$ at the top
ch04.obs.cliff: Angle 0° from a height $h > 0$ (horizontal throw): the $y$ shadow is a ball dropped from the same height, so both land together, whatever the launch speed
ch04.obs.range: From height 0 the range is largest at 45°, and 30° and 60° give the same range. From a height above 0 the best angle is below 45°
ch04.obs.g: Moon and Mars: same launch speed, smaller $g$, so longer flights and longer ranges
ch04.c.d.hodo: Velocity vectors drawn from one point; the direction their tip moves is $\vec a$
ch04.c.hodo.title: Velocity vectors (common tail)
ch04.c.goal.dir: Uniform circular motion: the speed is constant but the direction of the velocity keeps changing, so there is an acceleration
ch04.c.goal.a: The acceleration always points to the centre, with size $a = v^2/r$ (centripetal acceleration)
ch04.c.obs.perp: $\vec a \perp \vec v$: only the direction changes, not the speed
ch04.c.obs.hodo: Velocity circle: the tip of $\vec v$ runs around a circle of circumference $2\pi v$ once per period $T$, in the direction of $\vec a$, so $a = 2\pi v / T = v^2/r$
ch04.c.obs.scale: Same $r$, double $v$: $a$ is 4 times larger. Same $v$, double $r$: $a$ halves
ch04.c.assume: Acceleration arrows: length compressed at large $a$ so they never reach the centre. Order and direction are kept; exact values in the readouts
ch04.r.d.frame: View from the ground, or moving along with the water
ch04.r.p.heading: Heading
ch04.r.d.heading: Angle tilted upstream from straight across the river
ch04.r.d.vb: Speed $v_{BW}$ of the boat relative to the water
ch04.r.d.u: Speed $v_{WG}$ of the water relative to the ground
ch04.r.goal.add: Velocity depends on the frame: $\vec v_{BG} = \vec v_{BW} + \vec v_{WG}$ (B: boat, W: water, G: ground)
ch04.r.goal.frame: The same motion traces different paths in different frames
ch04.r.obs.straight: Heading 0°: the boat drifts downstream; the crossing time $W/v_{BW}$ does not depend on the current
ch04.r.obs.cancel: Heading 30° (default speeds): $v_{BW}\sin\theta = v_{WG}$ cancels the current, so the boat lands straight across but takes longer
ch04.r.obs.switch: Water frame: the boat goes straight along its heading while the banks move at $-\vec v_{WG}$
ch04.r.obs.up: Heading 60°: the boat lands upstream of its start
ch04.r.assume: River 20 m wide; the current is the same across the river
